page: Microsoft Azure E8-4ds_v6 is an x86_64 architecture server belonging to the Edsv6 family, virtualized via Microsoft Hyper-V. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at 4.2 GHz. The memory configuration is 64.0 GB, yielding a high resource density of 16.0 GB per core. Local storage is bundled with a 472 GB local disk, and the instance is Premium Storage capable. No GPUs are present on this configuration.

Benchmark data reveals strong single-core and single-threaded capabilities. The server achieves a strong Geekbench single-core score of 2170.0 and a single-threaded gzip compression speed of 31.35 GB/sec. However, multi-core and memory bandwidth metrics show limitations. The stress-ng multi-core CPU performance is weak at 3990.17, and memory bandwidth read-only tests for both small and large blocks fall into the bottom 25% tier. Large block memory write bandwidth is average at 25.89 GB/sec.

Given the high memory-to-vCPU ratio, this server is positioned for memory-intensive workloads that do not require massive parallel CPU scaling. It is suitable for database operations, caching layers, and text processing, supported by an average Passmark database score of 2890.86 and a strong Geekbench text processing score of 2554.0. Conversely, it is less suited for multi-threaded compilation, ray tracing, or medium-to-large LLM inference, where it registers weak to poor performance. The qualitative cost efficiency is characterized by high memory density relative to the compute footprint, making it a specialized option for memory-bound tasks.
